title: One October Holiday, Two Names: Columbus Day and Indigenous Peoples' Day
summary:
On October 12, 2026, people across the United States will observe a holiday that goes by two different names. Some will celebrate Columbus Day, while others will mark Indigenous Peoples' Day.

Columbus Day honors Christopher Columbus, an Italian explorer who arrived in the Americas on October 12, 1492. But his role in history has long been debated. Critics say his arrival led to the colonization and mistreatment of Native Americans.

Historians also point out that Columbus did not "discover" the Americas. Indigenous peoples had already been living there for thousands of years. He was not even the first European to reach North America. A Norse explorer named Leif Erikson reached the continent around A.D. 1000, almost 500 years before Columbus.

Because of these concerns, some states chose not to celebrate Columbus Day. Hawaii renamed the holiday Discoverers' Day in 1971 to honor its Polynesian founders. South Dakota began calling it Native American Day in 1990.

In 1977, a group of Native American leaders suggested the name "Indigenous Peoples' Day" to honor those who were mistreated by early settlers. In 1992, Berkeley, California, became the first city to make the change. Since then, more than 100 cities and several states have adopted Indigenous Peoples' Day. In 2021, President Joe Biden officially recognized the holiday and asked Americans to celebrate it on the second Monday of October, along with Columbus Day.

Not everyone agrees that a new name is needed. For many Italian Americans, Columbus Day is an important part of Italian Heritage Month, which is observed every October. They say the holiday celebrates Italian culture, not Columbus himself. Some have suggested calling it "Italian Heritage Day."

The debate shows that history can be complicated. No matter the name, the holiday is a time to think about the past.
why_it_matters: The debate shows how communities rethink history and decide whom to honor. It also shows that people can look at the same past in very different ways.

background_read: Columbus Day was created to remember Christopher Columbus's voyage across the Atlantic Ocean in 1492.
Indigenous peoples are the first peoples of a place, such as the many Native American nations who lived across the Americas long before Europeans arrived.
Columbus's voyages opened the way for European countries to set up colonies in the Americas, which changed Native American lives in many harmful ways.
Today, communities debate how one holiday can honor both the people who were already here and immigrant groups such as Italian Americans.
